turns.response_markdown:
Seasons change because Earth is tilted on its axis as it orbits the Sun, causing different parts of the planet to receive varying amounts of sunlight throughout the year.  
When a hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun it experiences warmer seasons, and when it is tilted away it experiences colder seasons.
